title: QPlanner: Cross-Cycle Orchestration for Hosted API & Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Nguyen
description: Purpose: create a repeatable quarterly planning runbook that aligns Hosted API product lanes with Model Catalog lifecycle (onboarding, rotation, deprecation) and maps OKRs/initiative-level commitments to enforceable canary and capacity hedges. Outcome: a two-way orchestration playbook (PM <-> Eng) that produces a tranche-aware roadmap with canary windows, gating criteria, and rollback policies for hosted model updates. Scope: hosted endpoints, model catalog rotations, canary cadence, capacity hedges for seasonal spikes, commit lanes for Dedicated customers, and runbook templates for Console owners to adopt.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook draft published in Confluence with template sections and owner assignments
Commitment lanes (Tier A/B/C) defined with capacity hedges and canary windows
Gating checklist created for model onboarding: eval pass rate thresholds, regression guardrails, perf sig-test targets
Cross-team cadence scheduled: quarterly roadmap sync + weekly execution triage for the sprint window
Automated dashboard links for token-cost and latency SLOs included in runbook
comments: 2026-02-10 - Aisha Nguyen: Kickoff note. Drafting initial outline; primary stakeholders identified: Hosted API PMs, Model Catalog owners, Eng leads for serving runtime, Console UX. Intent to produce a lightweight playbook focused on enforceable gates (quality, perf, capacity).

2026-02-15 - Jordan Patel: Scoped dependencies: ENG-12821 (canary rollout infra), ENG-12903 (capacity hedging autoscaler), and PM-47209 (hosted-endpoint contingency grid). Proposed triage meeting: 2026-02-18. Attached proto PRD: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qPlAN-example (work-in-progress).

2026-02-18 - Emily Cho (Eng Lead): Reviewed gating checklist. Feedback: require both absolute perf thresholds (p99 latency) and relative regression bounds (no >3% quality drop on baseline eval sets). Recommend adding a lightweight A/B rollback trigger tied to model-serving errors >0.5% over 15m. Linked internal RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Canary+Rollouts+RFC

2026-02-24 - Alex Rivera (Product Ops): Proposed canary windows matrix by region and tier; recommended scheduled canaries for low-traffic weekdays and burst windows for Dedicated customers. Provided sample cadence spreadsheet: https://sheets.google.com/some-cadence-sheet

2026-02-27 - Design feedback (Maya Lin): Suggest adding a Console UX checklist section so route owners can declare downstream metric expectations (token cost budgets, routing fallbacks). UI mocks linked: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UXmock

2026-02-28 - Jordan Patel: Incorporated Eng + Design feedback. Trade-offs documented: tightening gating thresholds reduces incident risk but increases canary friction and slower model rollout. Decision: adopt conservative early thresholds for Q1 trial, iterate to looser thresholds after two successful cycles. Added rollout timeline with three commitment lanes: Fast-Track, Standard, Deep-Canary.

2026-03-01 - Aisha Nguyen: Shared draft runbook in Confluence for stakeholder review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/QPlanner+Runbook. Next steps: 1) PM + Eng alignment session 2026-03-05, 2) finalize gating automations with Eng (ENG-12821), 3) produce Exec one-pager for Roadmap Review on 2026-03-12.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Model regressions slip to prod due to inadequate eval coverage. Mitigation: require a standard baseline eval suite for onboarding and mandate regression alerting tied to eval sets.
Risk: Capacity shortfall during seasonal spike. Mitigation: capacity hedges (burst pools) and pre-allocated Dedicated overflow; coordinate with infra for autoscaler policy (ENG-12903).
Risk: Cross-team misalignment on commitment lanes. Mitigation: run a monthly triage and a public commitments dashboard; escalate mismatches to product ops.
links: Related Linear: PM-47209 (contingency grid), ENG-12821 (canary infra)
